github.page_description: Install a GitHub App, control how Pull Requests show up inside Multica, and decide what your agents leave behind in commit history. GitHub uses a workspace-level App installation flow, unlike GitLab's enterprise connection form.
github.master_description_on: When off, every GitHub UI affordance is hidden and no new side-effects are written. Existing data is kept on the backend. Not a development team? Just turn it off here.
github.master_description_off: GitHub features are turned off. The PR sidebar, co-author trailer, and auto-link are paused. Data on the backend is not deleted.
github.gitlab_master_description_on: When off, GitLab issues, merge requests, repository context, and project routing stop syncing. Existing data is kept.
github.gitlab_master_description_off: GitLab features are turned off. Connection details are kept, but no GitLab sync writes run.
github.gitlab_master_description_unconnected: Save a GitLab connection before enabling GitLab features.
github.gitlab_feature_mr_sidebar_description: Show linked merge requests inside the issue detail sidebar.
github.gitlab_feature_auto_link_description: Scan an MR's branch, title, and description for issue identifiers and link them automatically.
github.gitlab_feature_co_author_description: Append a Co-authored-by trailer crediting the Multica agent on commits.
github.gitlab_feature_status_advance_descriptio: Move a linked issue to done when its merge request is merged.

github.disconnect_confirm_description: Multica will stop receiving webhooks for this installation. Existing PR mirrors and links are kept; reconnect any time to resume updates.

github.feature_pr_sidebar_description: Show linked pull requests inside the issue detail sidebar.

enterprise_integrations.title: Integration modules
enterprise_integrations.center_description: Review Git, ZenTao, and Lark connection status, sync health, and project binding summaries. Open each settings page for detailed configuration.
enterprise_integrations.description: Admins configure enterprise connections in this Multica workspace first; each member then binds their own external account and token. Here, workspace means the Multica workspace, not a GitLab, ZenTao, or Lark workspace.
enterprise_integrations.admin_required: Ask a Multica workspace admin to configure this enterprise connection first.
enterprise_integrations.secret_key_required: Set MULTICA_INTEGRATION_SECRET_KEY on the server before saving credentials.
enterprise_integrations.account_management_hint: Personal accounts are managed from My Account / Access Tokens.
enterprise_integrations.workspace_accounts_description: Accounts connected to this Multica workspace. Admins can remove accounts; members can view the mappings.
enterprise_integrations.workspace_accounts_empty: No external accounts are connected in this workspace yet.
enterprise_integrations.project_bindings_description: Bind Multica projects to external products, repositories, spaces, or drives and choose the sync directions.
enterprise_integrations.invalid_external_ref: External reference must be a valid JSON object.

gitlab.title: GitLab
gitlab.subtitle: GitLab issues, merge requests, repository context, and project routing.
gitlab.connection_help: Admins enter the enterprise GitLab root URL, for example https://gitlab.company.com. Members can bind their own GitLab accounts after this is saved.
gitlab.account_help: Enter the username or email GitLab uses for you so external assignees can be mapped to Multica members.
gitlab.credential_help: In GitLab, open avatar → Preferences → Access Tokens. For read-only sync, grant at least read_api; for outbound issue/comment creation, grant api.

zentao.title: ZenTao
zentao.subtitle: Bugs, stories, tasks, and product/project execution.
zentao.connection_help: Admins enter the ZenTao V2 API URL or enterprise gateway URL. Multica uses it to read products, projects, executions, bugs, stories, and tasks.
zentao.account_help: Enter your ZenTao account name so bugs, stories, and tasks assigned to you can be mapped to your Multica member.
zentao.credential_help: Create a token in ZenTao personal settings or Open API. If your company uses a V2/CLI gateway, use the personal token or service account token accepted by that gateway.

feishu.title: Lark
feishu.subtitle: Bot, IM, Docs, Wiki, and Drive knowledge sync.
feishu.account_placeholder: Lark user id, open_id, or email
feishu.connection_help: Admins usually keep the Lark Open Platform URL as https://open.feishu.cn for mainland Feishu, or configure the enterprise Lark endpoint for international tenants. Enterprise app, Drive, and Wiki scopes are configured under this connection.
feishu.account_help: Enter your Lark user id, open_id, or company email so IM, Docs, Wiki, and Drive permissions can map to this Multica member.
feishu.credential_help: Personal OAuth tokens should come from an authorization flow. For enterprise Drive/Wiki sync, admins should configure app_id/app_secret instead of asking members to paste long-lived secrets.

enterprise_integrations.feishu_app_secret_configured: Secret set — leave blank to keep
